rfi.description: Amnesty International has accused South Sudanese authorities and UN peacekeepers of failing to prevent a massacre earlier this year, despite advance warnings of an imminent attack.

rfi.title: Global Microsoft outage knocks out Outlook and other services
rfi.description: Microsoft’s Outlook email service has been down since late on Thursday, disrupting businesses and government agencies in 74 countries and territories. On Friday the company said the outage was caused by a heavy load on its infrastructure, rather than by malicious activity.

rfi.title: Algerian writer Kamel Daoud sentenced to five years over prize-winning novel
rfi.description: Franco-Algerian writer Kamel Daoud and his wife have each been sentenced to five years in prison by an Algerian court over allegations that his award-winning novel Houris drew on confidential medical information about a woman who survived an Islamist attack during the country's civil war in the 1990s.

rfi.title: Migration to wealthy countries slows for second year amid tougher rules
rfi.description: Legal migration to developed countries dropped for a second year in a row in 2025, down 1.6 percent compared to the previous year, as governments tightened rules for workers, students and refugees, according to an OECD report published Thursday. But the figures show sharply diverging trends – with big increases in Southern Europe and sharp declines in North America.

france24fr.description: L'Afrique peut-elle former ses propres élites sans les envoyer étudier à l'étranger ? Au Maroc, l'Université Mohammed VI Polytechnique (UM6P) s'impose parmi les établissements africains les mieux classés à l'international. Recherche, intelligence artificielle, robotique, agriculture : l'université mise sur des formations de pointe pour répondre aux défis du continent. Mais cette excellence est-elle accessible à tous ? Et ce modèle peut-il être reproduit ailleurs en Afrique ? Sa Benjamin Traoré,

france24fr.title: Présidence de la Francophonie : Louise Mushikiwabo "candidate jusqu'au bout"
france24fr.description: C’est une information révélée par nos confrères de Jeune Afrique : la France aurait demandé au Rwanda de retirer sa candidature pour le poste de secrétaire général de l’Organisation Internationale de la Francophone. Les pays membres sont en ce moment réunis au Cambodge et doivent choisir qui sera à la tête de l’OIF.  Et cela a bien évidemment fait réagir sur le continent…

france24fr.title: Acte V du mouvement social : des revendications variées, une affluence en baisse
france24fr.description: Lors de l'acte V du mouvement social qui ébranle la France, quelque 106 000 à 200 000 personnes ont défilé samedi dans toute la France, selon les chiffres du ministère de l'Intérieur et l'intersyndicale jeune (Union étudiante, USL, Fage, Unef). Quelques incidents se sont produits et des journalistes ont été agressés.

france24fr.title: Israël : Eisenkot accuse Netanyahu d'entraver la formation d'un gouvernement
france24fr.description: Alors que Benjamin Netanyahu plaide pour un gouvernement d'union nationale, son rival Gadi Eisenkot, chargé de former le prochain gouvernement israélien, a dénoncé samedi les "ruses" du Premier ministre sortant. Des discussions entre leurs partis sont déjà prévues dimanche.

france24fr.title: Éliminatoires de la CAN 2027 : l'Algérie s'impose de peu contre le Togo et conforte sa première place
france24fr.description: L'Algérie a dû s'employer pour faire céder une solide équipe du Togo (1-0), samedi lors de la troisième journée des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027. Longtemps en échec dans le dernier geste, les Fennecs ont finalement trouvé la faille sur un ballon d'Hadj Moussa déposé sur la tête de Bensebaïni en fin de match. Cette courte victoire permet aux Algériens de conforter leur place de leader de leur groupe (7 points) avant les trois dernières journées.

france24fr.title: Éliminatoires de la CAN 2027 : l'Algérie s'impose de peu contre le Togo et conforte sa première place
france24fr.description: L'Algérie a dû s'employer pour faire céder une vaillante équipe du Togo (1-0), samedi 14 novembre lors de la troisième journée des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027. Longtemps restés en échec dans le dernier geste, les Fennecs ont finalement trouvé la faille grâce à un ballon d'Hadj Moussa déposé sur la tête de Bensebaïni en fin de match. Cette courte victoire permet aux Algériens de conforter leur place de leader du groupe (7 points) avant le début de la quatrième journée.

france24fr.title: La cyberattaque d'une filiale de La Poste entraîne un vol de données touchant 22 millions de personnes
france24fr.description: Maileva, filiale du groupe La Poste, a été victime d'une cyberattaque mi-septembre ayant conduit au vol des coordonnées de 22 millions de personnes. L'an dernier, une cyberattaque revendiquée par des hackers prorusses avait déjà touché La Poste à quelques jours de Noël.

france24fr.title: Après l'échec du premier étage, SpaceX tente de rattraper le second étage de sa fusée Starship
france24fr.description: Après avoir renoncé vendredi à rattraper le premier étage de sa mégafusée Starship en raison d'un incident technique, l'entreprise SpaceX d'Elon Musk veut samedi tenter d'en récupérer le second après plus de 22 heures de vol, ce qui constituerait une prouesse technique.

france24fr.title: Macron dénonce "ceux qui veulent rationner" l’aide à l’Ukraine et "l’obliger à une paix injuste"
france24fr.description: Dans un message publié sur son compte X, Emmanuel Macron a estimé samedi que "rationner les moyens de l'Ukraine" était "la recette pour la guerre d'après". Le président de la République a appelé à ne pas diminuer les aides à l'Ukraine, comme la candidate du Rassemblement national Marine Le Pen l'a précédemment envisagé, si elle est élue.

france24fr.title: Ligue des nations : face à la Turquie, Mbappé et les Bleus en mission pour la qualification
france24fr.description: Renversée par l'Italie à Milan lors de la cinquième journée de Ligue des nations, l'équipe de France jouera sa qualification en quarts de finale face à la Turquie dimanche à Bordeaux. Malgré l'absence de nombreux cadres, notamment en défense, Zinédine Zidane devrait pouvoir compter sur le retour de son capitaine Kylian Mbappé pour retrouver des certitudes et décrocher une place en phase finale de la compétition.

france24fr.title: Francophonie : la RD Congo menace de quitter l'organisation
france24fr.description: Le XXe sommet de la Francophonie se tient les 15 et 16 novembre 2026 à Phnom Penh, au Cambodge. Quatre candidats sont en lice pour le secrétariat général de l'OIF, dans un contexte diplomatique tendu. La RD Congo menace notamment de reconsidérer sa place au sein de l'organisation si la Rwandaise Louise Mushikiwabo obtient un troisième mandat. Un dossier devenu prioritaire pour Paris. Les précisions d'Aurélie Bazzara-Kibangula.

france24fr.title: Victorin Lurel, sénateur PS de la Guadeloupe : "L'oisiveté est la mère de tous les vices"
france24fr.description: Chaque semaine, Judith Grimaldi reçoit un invité dans son émission "Avec Judith." Cette fois-ci, c'est le sénateur PS de la Guadeloupe Victorin Lurel. Il revient sur son parcours de vie, et réagit notamment au taux de chômage élevé en Guadeloupe ainsi qu'à la candidature à l'élection présidentielle de Teddy Riner.

france24fr.title: Rugby : exploit des Gallois, victorieux contre les All Blacks pour la première fois depuis 1953
france24fr.description: Le XV du Poireau a arraché une victoire historique face à la Nouvelle-Zélande, samedi à Cardiff, dans le cadre de la cinquième journée du Championnat des nations, mettant fin à une disette de 73 ans face aux All Blacks.

france24fr.title: De communiste à conseiller de Macron, le parcours de l'économiste Philippe Aghion
france24fr.description: Comme chaque semaine, Judith Grimaldi reçoit un invité dans son podcast "Avec Judith". Cette fois-ci, c'est Philippe Aghion, économiste français, prix Nobel d'économie 2025.

france24fr.title: Burkina Faso : mandats d'arrêt contre des journalistes et activistes en exil pour faits de "terrorisme"
france24fr.description: Les autorités du Burkina Faso ont annoncé avoir lancé des mandats d’arrêt contre une vingtaine de personnes en exil et demandé leur extradition. Des journalistes et un ancien pilier du régime de Blaise Compaoré sont notamment visés.

france24fr.title: Teddy Riner réfute être macroniste et qualifie de "baiser empoisonné" les félicitations de Macron
france24fr.description: Le judoka et désormais candidat à la présidentielle Teddy Riner s'est défendu samedi d'être macroniste, lors de son déplacement au salon du "Made in France". Le sportif de haut niveau a, en outre, qualifié de "baiser empoisonné" les félicitations d'Emmanuel Macron.

france24fr.title: Acte V contre la vie chère : une mobilisation aux revendications multiples
france24fr.description: Cinquième samedi de mobilisation contre la vie chère en France. Entre 50 et 60 cortèges sont attendus à travers le pays, autour de revendications variées mêlant pouvoir d'achat, climat et contestation du maintien de l'ordre. Cet "acte V" rassemble des profils et des mots d'ordre très différents. Sur place, notre journaliste Johan Bodin a notamment recueilli le témoignage de Mathis, membre d'Interfac, qui dénonce "l'installation d'un État policier en France".

france24fr.title: Attentat de Trappes : une liste d'élus de gauche retrouvée chez le suspect
france24fr.description: Dans l'enquête sur l'attentat de Trappes, les enquêteurs ont retrouvé chez Kevin T. une liste de personnalités de gauche et d'élus. Selon les premiers éléments, le suspect aurait également laissé des notes dans lesquelles il se disait "fier de ses actes" et affirmait vouloir "être pris en exemple". (France 2)

zeit.title: «Grand Theft Auto VI»: Ein gewaltiges Videospiel - Der lange Weg zu GTA 6
SPD: Bundespolitiker fordern Verbleib von Lars Klingbeil an Parteispitze
zeit.description: Bundesumweltminister Carsten Schneider hält einen Wechsel an der SPD-Spitze für unnötig. Fraktionschef Matthias Miersch warnt vor falschen Hoffnungen an einen neuen Mann.

zeit.title: SpaceX: Dieser Moment wird die Welt verändern – aber wie?
zeit.description: SpaceX fängt seine Superrakete Starship aus der Luft – ein Moment Raumfahrtgeschichte. Und der Schlusspunkt einer verrückten Wette gegen die Physik.

zeit.title: Phantasialand in Brühl: 15 Verletzte in Freizeitpark nach Microsoft-Panne
zeit.description: Ein Dosierungssystem hatte zu viel Chlor in einen Pool des Phantasialands gepumpt. Doch E-Mail-Warnungen kamen wegen der weltweiten Microsoft-Störung nicht an.

zeit.title: Raumfahrt: SpaceX fängt Riesen-Rakete Starship erstmals wieder auf
Abschiebezentren in Ruanda: Wie weit darf Deutschland bei Abschiebungen gehen?
zeit.description: Deutschland und mehrere EU-Staaten planen Abschiebezentren in Ruanda. Was bedeutet das für Asylsuchende? Und: Tschechien vor dem größten Protest seiner Geschichte

zeit.title: Luftverkehr in den USA: US-Regierung fordert nach Flugstopp Milliarden für Flugsicherung
zeit.description: Veraltete IT-Systeme haben den Flugverkehr in den USA lahmgelegt. Für die Modernisierung fordert der Verkehrsminister 50 Milliarden Dollar. Er warnt vor weiteren Pannen.

zeit.title: Auszeichnung: Preis für Verständigung und Toleranz für Tekkal und Moritz
Fußball-Nationalmannschaft: Abstieg nicht vom Tisch: Keine Portugal-Hilfe für Klopp
Jugendproteste: Erneute Gen-Z-Demonstrationen fallen deutschlandweit kleiner aus
zeit.description: In mehreren Städten haben erneut junge Menschen demonstriert, dieses Mal deutlich weniger als vor zwei Wochen. Für Freitag sind größere Proteste angekündigt.

zeit.title: Demonstrationen: Mehr als 100.000 Menschen protestieren in Frankreich
zeit.description: Erneut haben mehr als 100.000 Menschen in Frankreich für bessere Bildung und gegen hohe Lebenshaltungskosten demonstriert. Mehr als 200 Menschen wurden festgenommen.

zeit.title: Demonstrationen: Hunderte ziehen bei Gen-Z-Demo durch Berlin - 22 Festnahmen
Basketball: Towers zittern sich zum Sieg gegen Würzburg

nzz.title: «Als Bundesrat ungeeignet»: Alt-Richter warnen vor SVP-Kandidat Thomas Aeschi
nzz.description: Thomas Aeschi hat beste Chancen, von der SVP für den Bundesrat nominiert zu werden. Doch sein Verhältnis zur Justiz könnte ihm zum Verhängnis werden. Zudem wirft ein Dokument Fragen auf zu seiner Taktiererei.

nzz.title: Wird das Starship nun komplett wiederverwendbar? Die obere Stufe des Starship ist sicher zu seiner Startrampe in Texas zurückgekehrt
nzz.description: Die Sensation ist geglückt. Nachdem die untere Stufe des Starship am Freitag noch im Meer landete, verlief die Landung der oberen Stufe am Samstag nach Plan. Für SpaceX und die Raumfahrt ist das ein echter Durchbruch.

nzz.title: Im Visier von ausländischen Agenten: Wenn der chinesische Panda-Zug plötzlich aussieht wie die Kiss-Züge von Stadler
nzz.description: Der Fall Nvidia zeigt, wie verbreitet Wirtschaftsspionage ist. Mit ihren Hightech-Produkten sind auch Schweizer Firmen attraktive Ziele. Doch sie unterschätzten die Risiken, sagt ein Experte.

nzz.title: Von China-Drohnen, Agenten mit Diplomatenpass und «intellectual traps»: Was treiben Pekings Spione in der Schweiz?
nzz.description: Die Nvidia-Affäre wirft ein Schlaglicht auf das Vorgehen von Chinas Agenten, auch in Genf oder Zürich. Jetzt rüsten sich Armee, Hochschulen und Politik gegen die Gefahr. Doch reicht das?

nzz.title: Sind Andermatt und Crans-Montana Millionengräber? Vail-Resorts-Aktionäre rebellieren und werfen dem Unternehmen Missmanagement vor
nzz.description: Der amerikanische Skigigant taumelt. Der Börsenwert hat sich innert fünf Jahren halbiert. In Europa kassiert Vail Absage um Absage – zuletzt in Österreich. Die Expansion steht auf der Kippe.

nzz.title: Vom Berner Oberland nach Moskau: Schweizer Scharfschützenmunition gelangt illegal nach Russland
nzz.description: Recherchen zeigen, dass Ruag-Munition über dubiose Zwischenhändler verschoben wurde. Ein internationales Netzwerk hat die Patronen via Balkan in Putins Reich geschmuggelt. Der Fall hat politische Sprengkraft.

nzz.title: Korruptionsverdacht gegen Ex-Minister Orbans: Ungarische Ermittler finden Bargeld in Millionenhöhe – vergraben im Wald und versteckt in Lagerhallen
nzz.description: Peter Magyars Amt für Vermögensrückgewinnung entdeckt Bündel voller Geld im Gesamtwert von 16 Millionen Franken. Der Fall setzt Orbans Partei unter Druck.

nzz.title: Wie es zum Flug-Shutdown in den USA kam: wenn KI-Software auf zwanzig Jahre alte Server und auf Disketten trifft
nzz.description: Es war einer der schwersten Ausfälle der amerikanischen Luftfahrtgeschichte: Weil veraltete Router unter einem neuen Sicherheitsupdate zusammenbrachen, standen am Freitag die Radarschirme still. Der Flugverkehr musste im ganzen Land für Stunden ausgesetzt werden.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Die USA nach den Midterms: Demokrat gewinnt Gouverneurswahl in Alaska – erstmals wieder seit 1998
nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus der amerikanischen Innenpolitik im Ticker.

nzz.title: Er nannte Jensen Huang ein «nationales Heiligtum»: Der US-Handelsminister Howard Lutnick gerät in den Sog des Nvidia-Skandals
nzz.description: Finanzminister Scott Bessent wirft Handelsminister Howard Lutnick vor, Exporte der Hochleistungschips von Nvidia nach China nicht verhindert zu haben. Nun untersucht auch der Senat die Affäre.

nzz.title: Dreiergipfel in Shenzhen: Peking organisiert ein Treffen zwischen Donald Trump, Xi Jinping und Wladimir Putin
nzz.description: Das Weisse Haus bestätigte die hochrangige Zusammenkunft. Das Problem ist, dass die drei Staatsoberhäupter mit unterschiedlichen Absichten in die Gespräche gehen werden – das Thema ist weiterhin offen.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN KULTUR - Sandra Hüller doppelt für Europäischen Filmpreis nominiert
nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus dem Feuilleton.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: USA sollen Selenski Nato-Beitritt im Tausch gegen Rückzug aus Donbass vorgeschlagen haben +++ Ukrainischer Drohnenangriff tötet Familie in Westrussland
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Chaos an den Flughäfen – die Bilder zum Flugstopp in den USA
nzz.description: Ein technischer Ausfall hat am Freitagabend den gesamten amerikanischen Flugverkehr lahmgelegt. Über 13 000 Flüge waren vom landesweiten Startverbot der Luftfahrtbehörde FAA betroffen.

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - Nvidia und Anthropic machen die Börse nervös – ein 3600-Milliarden-Fonds-Chef gibt Entwarnung: «Die Umsätze sind sehr real»
nzz.description: Die Krise bei Nvidia und die Furcht vor einer KI-Blase verunsichern die Anleger. Mike Gitlin, CEO des Fondsriesen Capital Group, hält Vergleiche mit der Finanzkrise 2008 jedoch für unbegründet.

nzz.title: Vier Stunden Stillstand: Ein landesweiter Flugstopp stürzt die USA in chaotische Zustände
nzz.description: Die amerikanische Luftfahrtbehörde (FAA) stoppte am Freitagabend sämtliche Abflüge im ganzen Land. Mehr als 13 000 Flüge waren betroffen. Die Regierung macht technische Probleme im veralteten Flugkontrollsystem verantwortlich.

spiegel.title: Hamas-Kommandeur im Gazastreifen getötet
spiegel.description: Seit Monaten gilt eine Waffenruhe zwischen Israel und der Hamas. Doch die Attacken gehen weiter. Jetzt soll ein ranghoher Hamas-Kommandeur nach einem israelischen Luftangriff im Süden des Gazastreifens gestorben sein.

spiegel.title: Kabel- und Routertausch soll Flugchaos verursacht haben – Tausende weitere Flüge gestrichen
spiegel.description: Auch einen Tag nach dem Startverbot auf fast allen US-Airports ist der Flugverkehr stark gestört. 4000 weitere Verbindungen wurden gestrichen. Auslöser war offenbar die Installation neuer Kabel und Router in einem betagten IT-System.

spiegel.title: SpaceX fängt Starship-Rakete erstmals am Startturm wieder auf
spiegel.description: Wichtiger Schritt in der Raumfahrtentwicklung: Elon Musks Unternehmen SpaceX hat es geschafft, die obere Stufe des »Starship«-Systems nach einem Testflug wieder aufzufangen. Ein voller Erfolg war das Manöver trotzdem nicht.

spiegel.title: Masern: USA verlieren offenbar Status als masernfreies Land
spiegel.description: Die USA werden wohl nicht mehr als masernfrei eingestuft. Wie mehrere amerikanische Medien berichten, verliert das Land seinen Status – nach mehr als 25 Jahren.

spiegel.title: Bundesliga der Frauen: Bayern München dominiert den VfL Wolfsburg beim 4:1 im Topspiel
spiegel.description: Wolfsburg gegen Bayern München, es sollte das Topspiel in der Fußball-Bundesliga der Frauen sein. Tatsächlich zeigte die Partie: Bei den Frauen herrschen längst die gleichen Verhältnisse wie bei den Männern.

spiegel.title: ME/CFS bei Kindern: Wie schwer die Krankheit das Leben verändert
spiegel.description: Annabelle kann ihren Kopf nicht heben, verträgt kein Licht und wird künstlich ernährt. Ihre Schwester Mathilda wacht nachts vor Schmerzen auf. Die Mutter pflegt beide rund um die Uhr. Hat die Familie noch Hoffnung auf Heilung?

spiegel.title: Azubis aus Vietnam in Deutschland: Acht Menschen in einem Raum, Lohn oft verweigert - SPIEGEL TV
spiegel.description: Sie kamen nach Deutschland für eine Ausbildung in der Pflege. Was sie erlebt haben, gleicht einem Albtraum: Zusammengepfercht zu acht in einem Zimmer, unregelmäßige bis keine Vergütung, Kündigungsdrohungen für Nachfragen nach dem Lohn.

spiegel.title: Phantasialand in Brühl: Wegen Microsoft-Ausfall Chlorpanne zu spät entdeckt – 15 Verletzte
spiegel.description: Wegen des Microsoft-Ausfalls ist offenbar ein Hotelpool des Phantasialands zur Gefahr geworden: Dem Wasser wurde laut dem Freizeitpark zu viel Chlor beigemischt, doch das Alarmsystem versagte.

spiegel.title: SPD: Hubertus Heil will für Parteivorsitz kandidieren
spiegel.description: Bei der SPD zeichnet sich ein Machtkampf ab: Ex-Arbeitsminister Hubertus Heil will sich beim Bundesparteitag im Januar zum Chef der Sozialdemokraten wählen lassen. Damit wächst der Druck auf Amtsinhaber Lars Klingbeil.

spiegel.title: Eurovision Song Contest Asia: Philippinische Sängerin Carmelle gewinnt erste Ausgabe
spiegel.description: Die Teilnehmerin aus den Philippinen hat die erste Ausgabe des asiatischen ESC gewonnen. Mit ihrem Song »Sobra-Sobra« siegte sie beim Finale in Thailand gegen Konkurrenten aus zehn anderen Ländern.

spiegel.title: Arbeiten mit KI: Diese Menschen verdienen Geld mit Prompts, seitenlangen Prompts
spiegel.description: Alle reden von KI – aber was macht es eigentlich mit jemandem, den ganzen Tag mit KI zu reden? Promptwriter wie Fabian Scholz können mit ihrer Arbeit viel Geld verdienen. Oder sich darin verlieren.

spiegel.title: Eurowings-Interna: Was in der Luft gesagt werden darf – und was nicht
spiegel.description: Das Personal an Bord soll die Lage schönreden. Interne Dokumente zeigen, wie streng die Vorgaben für Durchsagen in der Luft sind. Und warum aus Gewittern »Regenschauer« werden.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz in Schleswig-Holstein: Der Kanzler meidet das S-Wort
spiegel.description: Friedrich Merz drückt sich bei der CDU in Schleswig-Holstein um den Streit über die Stromsteuer herum. Umso deutlicher macht der Gastgeber, Ministerpräsident Daniel Günther, was die Partei erwartet.

spiegel.title: Midterms in den USA: Demokrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins gewinnt Gouverneurswahl in Alaska
spiegel.description: Elf Tage nach den US-Wahlen steht der Sieger im nördlichsten Bundesstaat fest: Alaska wird künftig von einem Demokraten regiert – dem jüngsten Gouverneur, den der Bundesstaat je hatte.

spiegel.title: Tuberkulose-Bericht: Kraftakt gegen tödlichste Infektionskrankheit der Welt
spiegel.description: Tuberkulose tötet mehr als eine Million Menschen pro Jahr, in Europa erkrankten 2025 etwa 180.000 Menschen. Wegen starker Kürzungen wurde das Schlimmste befürchtet. Doch stark betroffene Länder stellen sich dem Kampf.

spiegel.title: Kroatien: Auswanderer wagt mit 61 den Neustart auf der Insel Brac
spiegel.description: Mit seiner Frau und drei Kindern zog Bernd Alexander Mansholt aus Oldenburg los, »um die schönste Insel der Welt zu finden«. Jetzt, 22 Jahre und viele Schicksalsschläge später, hat er sie gefunden – aber nicht dort, wo er sie vermutet hatte.

spiegel.title: Weltklimakonferenz in der Türkei: Deutsche Chefunterhändlerin erklärt ihren Kurs
spiegel.description: Nur ein Minister fliegt zum Klimagipfel, die Klimahilfen für arme Länder schrumpfen, die Golfstaaten bremsen jeden Fortschritt. Die deutsche Verhandlungsführerin Heike Henn erklärt, warum sie trotzdem kämpft.

spiegel.title: Ungarn: Bei Korruptionsermittlungen gegen Ex-Minister 17,7 Millionen Euro sichergestellt
spiegel.description: Im Wald vergraben, in Lagerhallen versteckt: Ungarns Antikorruptionsbehörde hat bei Ermittlungen gegen einen früheren Minister der Regierung Orbán Bargeld in Millionenhöhe gefunden – und stundenlang gezählt.

observador.title: As notícias das 2h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: 1h. Acampada. PSP vai adotar "postura de prevenção"
observador.description: A decisão da pernoita foi tomada pela Acampada de Lisboa num dia marcado pela manifestação pelo direito à habitação. Ainda, no futebol, Portugal sofreu uma pesada derrota frente à Dinamarca.

observador.title: Da Real Barraca à Acampada da República
observador.description: Dom José aterrorizado com o terramoto não mais quis dormir sob telha e enfiou-se na Real Barraca, já Seguro com medo de desagradar à rua de esquerda levou a barraca para Belém.

observador.title: De Gaulle e as democracias europeias
observador.description: De Gaulle fala mais ao problema central das democracias europeias actuais do que o desfile penoso dos políticos sem grandeza e dos intelectuais sem visão a que temos direito.

observador.title: Seguro e o fim do tripartidarismo em Portugal
observador.description: Seguro normalizou o Chega. Não havendo lugar para três grandes partidos no sistema, o fim do tripartidarismo será a queda de um, pelo que é provável que os três desejem uma legislatura até 2029.

observador.title: Uma velha armadilha e um novo poder
observador.description: Já vai sendo tempo de Rutte perceber que este discurso do papão russo na Europa do Sul é contraproducente, até porque uma resposta possível a ele é advogar o neutralismo

observador.title: A Quarta-Feira do Juízo Final
observador.description: Acho que os portugueses adoram o fim do mundo porque não acreditam mesmo nele. Por isso o planeamento lhes sai tão natural.

observador.title: 00h. Homenagem a Ronaldo estragada por goleada dinamarquesa
observador.description: Portugal sofre a maior derrota em casa ao perder 4-1 frente à Dinamarca. Jorge Jesus afirma que os dinamarqueses foram melhores do que a equipa das quinas. João Palhinha pede desculpa aos adeptos.

observador.title: França: anatomia de uma tempestade perfeita
observador.description: Os limites do Estado Social europeu

observador.title: O elogio da loucura
observador.description: O que assistimos não é activismo, mas atavismo político, tirado de 1917.

observador.title: Projete-se o futuro de Portugal
observador.description: Cabe-nos a nós projetar o futuro. Enquanto jovem, mas principalmente enquanto portuguesa, continuarei a sonhar com um futuro melhor, porque Portugal é mais do que os problemas que hoje enfrenta.

observador.title: Golden Visa: investimento, mas acima de tudo confiança
observador.description: Portugal tem vantagens reconhecidas para atrair capital, mas precisam de ser acompanhadas por um enquadramento legislativo que transmita confiança.

observador.title: "Magalhães": mais uma oportunidade perdida
observador.description: Lamento que o Estado português tenha contribuído para financiar uma obra tão pobre e redutora relativamente ao período mais extraordinário da nossa história.

observador.title: A responsabilidade política não prescreve com uma demissão
observador.description: O caso de Ricardo Correia de Matos, agora detido no âmbito da operação “Batas & Betão”, é particularmente revelador das questões que importa colocar.

observador.title: Ninguém atacou o supermercado

phys-org.title: Urban expansion causes ecological collapse in streams in the São Paulo Metropolitan Area
phys-org.description: The advance of urbanization in the São Paulo Metropolitan Area in Brazil is causing the collapse of food webs in local streams. A study published in August in the journal Nature Cities reveals that the impact of the metropolis goes far beyond a simple reduction in species. Degradation selectively eliminates organisms based on their size and simplifies ecological interactions. Networks of 190 connections plummet to just three.

phys-org.title: A dead star is flashing radio waves every 8 minutes, and its partner looks a lot like the sun
phys-org.description: Since 2022, astronomers have been puzzling over a new kind of cosmic object called long-period radio transients. These are objects that emit bright flashes of radio waves into space every few minutes to every few hours. Some have been traced back to binary systems consisting of a small, dim, cool star called a red dwarf in orbit with a stellar remnant called a white dwarf.

phys-org.title: Does your culture shape how you look at art? What an eye‑tracking study in Sudan revealed
phys-org.description: Today, Old Dongola is an abandoned settlement on the banks of the Nile in northern Sudan. Hundreds of years ago, however, this place looked very different.

phys-org.title: NASA's Voyager 1 closes in on a light-day in interstellar space for a new distance record
phys-org.description: NASA's Voyager 1 is about to become humanity's first object to reach one light-day from Earth as it pushes ever deeper into interstellar space.

phys-org.title: A cosmic magnifying glass could reveal the same supernova two more times in roughly 70 years
phys-org.description: Thanks to the gravitational lensing caused by a massive galaxy cluster and high-resolution images from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), astronomers discovered an exploding star when the universe was 4.9 billion years old. The discovery paper, posted to the arXiv preprint server on Oct. 23, presents a prediction for when the rest of the distorted images of SN Ares will arrive.

phys-org.title: Some of the oldest rocks ever discovered shed light on Earth's early history
phys-org.description: Earth is approximately 4.5 billion years old, according to estimates. However, rocks dating back to the planet's earliest days are extremely rare. Hence the excitement over the discovery in northern China of some of the oldest known rocks on Earth, dating back 3.95 billion years. And one of the reasons for all the attention is that they're revealing new clues about how Earth's crust formed and evolved.

phys-org.title: World's largest freshwater lake is recovering after decades of decline
phys-org.description: Lake Baikal in Siberia holds around 20% of the world's surface freshwater, making it the most voluminous freshwater lake (Lake Superior on the United States–Canada border is the largest by surface area). This makes the lake one of the most important environments for biodiversity—in fact, it was designated a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1996 because of this. Yet it has shown considerable decline over the last century, with aridification spreading across East Asia.

phys-org.title: Archaeologists shed new light on wealth and status among Europe's early herders
phys-org.description: How unequal were prehistoric societies? And how can archaeologists measure wealth in cultures that left behind no written records, no tax registers and no census data?

phys-org.title: A common food emulsifier could solve one of rocketry's oldest fuel problems
phys-org.description: In propulsion system design, engineers have long faced a trade-off between solid and liquid rocket fuels. Each has advantages and disadvantages, and in an effort to try to min/max the efficacy of different types of fuel, researchers have long placed an emphasis on a hybrid between solids and liquids—in other words, they've been working with gels. Unfortunately, gels have their own sets of problems to deal with.

phys-org.title: Alaska laments decline of its prized salmon populations
phys-org.description: In his Alaskan community, fisherman Bob Candopoulos has long welcomed tourists to his business that's showcased by a sign featuring a king salmon.

phys-org.title: California steels for storms that could trigger massive waves, flooding
phys-org.description: California was bracing Friday for a storm series packing heavy rain and surf that could once again flood coastal communities and potentially send monster waves pounding shores.

phys-org.title: SpaceX's Starship set for return to Earth after booster catch aborted

phys-org.title: SpaceX's Starship soars into orbit after booster explosion prevents an unprecedented double catch
phys-org.description: SpaceX's attempt to recover its entire Starship back at the launch pad was thwarted when the booster fell into the Gulf of Mexico and exploded Friday, but the spacecraft still soared into orbit in its boldest test yet.

phys-org.title: The role of social relationships in scaling agricultural innovations: A dimension that remains underreported in research
phys-org.description: A study published in Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems reveals that, although partnerships and institutional collaboration feature prominently in climate-oriented agricultural research, their relationship with the scaling of innovations is rarely explicitly documented. The findings highlight the need to better understand the role of social relationships to strengthen the design, monitoring and evaluation of scaling processes.

phys-org.title: Heavier-than-expected electron behavior may explain slower electrical flow in alpha-gallium oxide
phys-org.description: Power electronic devices help control the flow of electricity and convert it into forms needed by different machines, such as electric vehicles, renewable energy systems and industrial equipment. Semiconductor materials that can withstand high voltages, carry electricity efficiently and release heat effectively would make these devices more efficient and reliab

phys-org.title: Fiji petrel eludes 10-day search as communities aim to protect bird's habitat
phys-org.description: A new study details scientists' search for one of the planet's rarest birds in the waters off Fiji's Gau Island. Spanning 10 days, the expedition yielded no verified sightings of the critically endangered Fiji petrel, one of the world's most elusive birds. Fewer than 50 individuals are believed to remain on Earth.

phys-org.title: Unstable plasma heats itself with waves it generates, experiments reveal
phys-org.description: Fusion power is expected to be a sustainable energy source that emits no carbon dioxide during electricity generation. To achieve this, research is underway worldwide to confine high-temperature plasma using magnetic fields. To initiate a fusion reaction, high-energy particles or waves must be injected from outside to heat the plasma to extremely high temperatures.

undark.title: Australia’s Social Media Ban Has Not Worked — For Now
undark.description: New data coming out of Australia suggests that bans alone may not be an effective enough deterrent to stop children from using social media. But the research faces limitations. What does that mean for other countries considering similar restrictions?

undark.title: Body Snatchers and the Murky Process of Whole-Body Donation

The result is reminiscent of the body-snatching practices of years past.

undark.title: Book Review: The Bizarre Frontiers of Product Testing

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors
undark.description: Around 70 percent of people with cancer today will live for more than five years after their diagnosis. They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?
undark.description: Brazil has plans to repave a neglected 550-mile road in the South American rainforest to help connect the region and boost economic growth. But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: Interview: The Nerve That Could Transform Medicine
undark.description: Kevin Tracey, a researcher and neurosurgeon whose team discovered the vagus nerve’s link to the immune system more than two decades ago, has developed an electrical implant to stimulate the nerve in an effort to help rheumatoid arthritis sufferers who currently have difficulty taking medications.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds
undark.description: This year’s spring migration in North America unveiled real-time measures at a higher resolution than ever before. On one night, for instance, 156 million birds appeared in the skies, outpacing the forecasted total by 20 million. And researchers figured that out thanks to AI.

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency
undark.description: After years of limited oversight, the FDA sent warnings to more than 2,200 clinical trial sponsors about missing results, which were supposed to be uploaded to an official public database. Experts have pushed for greater transparency.

undark.title: Book Review: An Optimistic Defense of Uncertainty in Science
undark.description: At an uncertain moment in the sciences, Stuart Firestein argues in favor of optimism in “It Could Be Otherwise,” since uncertainty leaves room for possibility, and possibility drives curiosity, imagination, and the agency to study the peculiarities of the natural world.

The first sentences, about the writer Robert Cohn, have a tang of anti-Semitism, one that only becomes stronger later on as the narrator…

public-dom.title: Soldiers of Misfortune: The Drawings of Urs Graf the Elder
public-dom.description: A mercenary and miscreant, the Swiss Renaissance artist Urs Graf lived the violence and vice he summoned on his drafting table. Miya Tokumitsu introduces us to his astonishing drawings of soldiers and sex workers, and finds an impotent melancholy within these often nightmarish scenes.

public-dom.title: Last Order Dates for the Holiday Season
public-dom.description: The recommended cut-off dates to order from our shop by to ensure delivery in time for Dec 25th.

public-dom.title: The Triumph of Labour: Walter Crane’s Cartoons for the Cause (1896)
public-dom.description: Socialist illustrations intended as party favours for participants in the International Workers’ Congress.

public-dom.title: D. W. Griffith’s A Corner in Wheat (1909)
public-dom.description: D. W. Griffith’s moral tale of agricultural greed, borrowing from Frank Norris’ antimonopolist fictions.

public-dom.title: Slavdom Unearthed: Marian Wawrzeniecki’s Neopagan Paintings (1891–1923)
public-dom.description: A neopagan visual archive meant to rival the iconic power of the Christian West.

public-dom.title: Wonderful Weather: Floods and Foreboding in 17th-Century Britain
public-dom.description: When the Bristol Channel flooded in 1607, it was not just one of the worst natural disasters in British history, it was also a sign, for many, that they had strayed from the path of God. Erik Crnkovich examines the overlap of miraculous weather and the early modern printing industry, which cultivated a thirst for all things occult, exotic, and odd.

public-dom.title: Albrecht Dürer’s Monument to the Vanquished Peasants (1525)
public-dom.description: The design for a difficult-to-interpret monument that was never intended to be built.

public-dom.title: “Earth Not a Globe”: Parallax’s Zetetic Astronomy (1865)
public-dom.description: A book more or less responsible for the revival of Flat Earth theories in the modern period.

public-dom.title: Immortal Beloved: Krishna and Rādhā Exchanging Clothes (ca. 1700–1900)
public-dom.description: Indian images that grapple with the unbearable fact that lover and beloved are not one.

public-dom.title: “Men with Queer Nerves”: The Jumping Frenchmen of Maine
public-dom.description: In the late nineteenth century, visitors to Maine observed something strange: French-Canadian lumberjacks who, at the slightest stimulus, seemed to jump, strike out with their limbs, or mimic languages they could not speak. Ross Bullen introduces us to these so-called “Jumping Frenchmen” and to their greatest investigator, George M. Beard, who saw a link in their behavior between religious frenzy and neurasthenia.

public-dom.title: Rudolf Kalvach’s Wiener Werkstätte Postcards (1907)
public-dom.description: Postcards that summon medieval grotesques and brightly coloured folk art, but also feel distinctly modern.

public-dom.title: Paul Carus’ The History of the Devil and the Idea of Evil (1899)
public-dom.description: A history of the Evil One, from the earliest times to the present.

public-dom.title: The Alchemical Transformations of the Mutus Liber (1677)
public-dom.description: Carl Jung’s copy of the “mute book”, an alchemical manual charting (through a series of images) the “humid way” of forging the Philosopher’s Stone.

public-dom.title: Philip Sidney and the Extreme (Dis)graces of the Parenthesis
public-dom.description: Erasmus called them “little moons” and George Puttenham praised them as “figures of tolerable disorder” (if used not too often “nor too thick”). For Philip Sidney, they were simply indispensable. Florence Hazrat introduces us to the uncontested early modern king of brackets and to his romance Arcadia, which abruptly ends, like its author’s life, hanging on a parenthesis.

public-dom.title: “There is Nothing but Immortality!”: Walt Whitman and The Book of Heavenly Death (1905)
public-dom.description: Choice excerpts from *Leaves of Grass* that speak to Whitman’s conception of immortality.

public-dom.title: Anatomy Unzipped: John of Arderne’s Sweden Scroll (ca. 1425–35)
public-dom.description: Early surgical diagrams that present patients prying themselves open for our anatomical gaze.

public-dom.title: In Company Style: Illustrations from James Skinner’s Kitāb-i tashrīḥ al-aqvām (1825)
public-dom.description: An illuminated Persian manuscript about customs, culture, and caste, written by an enigmatic figure of the early British Raj.

public-dom.title: Veronese's Dogs
public-dom.description: “Oh, if I could only pray”, Luther once said of his dog Tölpel, “the way this dog watches the meat”. Attending to attentive canine figures in half a dozen paintings by Paolo Veronese, Thomas W. Laqueur explores the work of an artist whose love of dogs landed him in hot water with the Inquisition.

eurozine.title: Before social media, there were postcards
Nacionalistický sen o realite vytvára umelá inteligencia
eurozine.description: Rýchle, lacné, repetitívne a účinné: krajne pravicové príspevky generované umelou inteligenciou zaplavujú internet a sociálne siete. Za gýčovou fasádou sa skrývajú paralely s nacistickou propagandou. Rozdiel je v tom, že tvorba obrazov v rôznych formátoch, je dnes dostupná pre každého a zákernejšia, ako ukazuje slovenské hnutie Brat za Brata.

eurozine.title: Obstinacy
Ett gott liv i dåliga tider
eurozine.description: Sociologen Richard Sennett reflekterar i denna essä, utifrån de personliga erfarenheter hans föräldrar gjorde under McCarthyeran, över hur olika former av förföljelse och totalitärt styre lämnar olika arv efter sig. Som enskild människa måste man leva igenom även mycket dåliga tider. Strategierna kan vara många. Kanske måste, menar Sennett, socialismen sätta det sociala tillbaka på agendan, för att förbereda sig för en tid efter Trump.

eurozine.title: A good life in bad times
Sudety, ztracený ráj?
eurozine.description: Nejznámější stereotyp o Sudetech říká, že po vyhnání Němců nově příchozí obyvatelstvo k těmto regionům nic nepoutalo, což je hlavní důvod jejich kolapsu. Zapomíná se přitom nejen na roli, kterou v tom sehrál bývalý režim, ale i na propad, jenž přišel v devadesátých letech. Jaký sociální obsah se skrývá za zeměpisným pojmem Sudety?

eurozine.title: Sudety: A paradise lost?
Reshaping and reconciliation
Democracy unfolding

eurozine.description: Vydáním České cikánské rapsodie v roce 2016 získal historik Jan Tesař nové čtenáře ještě po své osmdesátce. V žádném z politických režimů, které zažil, však nepsal příběhy v souladu s výklady minulosti, o něž se opírala moc. Platilo to i pro témata odboje a vztahu české společnosti k autoritářství.

proj-syn.title: The Rare-Earth Game
proj-syn.description: China will probably not impose a rare-earth embargo, but it will keep the specter of one alive. And the West will probably not achieve self-sufficiency in this critical sector, but it will keep seeking to reduce its vulnerability to a supply shock through expensive capacity duplication and stockpiles.

proj-syn.title: Why Research Matters
proj-syn.description: Over the past 21 months, in the country that has leveraged research to greatest effect, the government is slashing funding for it, closing centers where it is done, politicizing grant-making decisions, and bullying its single biggest engine: universities. The costs will be far greater than many realize.

proj-syn.title: Africa Needs a Different Kind of Climate Finance
proj-syn.description: Roughly half of the climate finance that flows to Africa comes in the form of debt, with multilateral and bilateral development-finance institutions often lending at commercial rates to economies already struggling to carry the added costs. To maximize fiscal space, the instruments used to deliver climate finance need to change.

proj-syn.title: Effective Climate Action Requires Capable States
proj-syn.description: With delegations from around the world gathering for another international climate conference, the question today is not whether governments should do more to address the climate crisis, but whether they even have the capabilities to do so. After 40 years of free-market orthodoxy, many simply do not.

proj-syn.title: Why Is Mexico Defying Latin America’s Right Turn?
proj-syn.description: How Mexico’s left has managed to retain strong support is a key question of contemporary Latin American politics. The most likely answer centers on the ruling Morena party’s pragmatic brand of left-wing politics, which combines bold redistributive policies, greater security, and a willingness to compromise in the name of both.

proj-syn.title: The Digital-Currency Divide
proj-syn.description: The rush to develop central bank digital currencies has slowed as underwhelming demand and mounting costs have given governments second thoughts. But while the Federal Reserve and other central banks have shelved their plans, the European Central Bank is pressing ahead with its digital euro.

proj-syn.title: The ASEAN Paradox
proj-syn.description: As the Association of Southeast Asian Nations gathers for its 49th Summit, several rifts have exposed the group’s institutional shortcomings. But amid a fracturing global order, ASEAN must choose: turn its convening authority into concerted action or be reduced to an arena for great-power rivalry.

proj-syn.title: Medical AI Needs Bedside Manners
proj-syn.description: Even the most accurate medical AI tools have little value if they make patients uneasy or doctors find them too cumbersome. A comfort-by-design approach could overcome these obstacles by involving patients and practitioners in development and ensuring that new systems work with existing medical practices.

proj-syn.title: Reviving the Legacy of Reykjavík
proj-syn.description: As nuclear threats grow, AI accelerates, and international law comes under strain, the world urgently needs a renewed commitment to dialogue. Today's leaders can find a template in the landmark 1986 summit between then US President Ronald Reagan and Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s AI Dreams Exceed Its Grid
proj-syn.description: Europe is racing to expand its AI data-center capacity, but its power grids are already strained, and local communities are increasingly pushing back against new construction. Achieving technological sovereignty will require less grandstanding and more practical solutions that make better use of existing resources.

proj-syn.title: What the US Midterms Could Mean for AI
proj-syn.description: Now that the Democrats will hold sizable majorities in both chambers of the US Congress, they have an opening to push for long-overdue legislation to steer AI development toward the common good. Private companies should not have the power to decide unilaterally which risks the public will bear.

proj-syn.title: Let’s Publish AI-Generated Articles!
proj-syn.description: Peer-reviewed academic journals exist to advance our knowledge and understanding by publishing the best work being done in a given field. If that is the goal, and the best reviewers—both human and AI—agree that an article generated by AI meets that standard, why should a journal's editors reject it?

proj-syn.title: The AI Industry Should Make Something People Want
proj-syn.description: AI companies have alienated Americans by forcing them to bear the costs of their products while treating their consent as optional. With voters across the United States rejecting data centers, the incoming Congress has an opportunity to enact meaningful regulation and hold the industry accountable.

proj-syn.title: It’s the Corruption, Stupid
proj-syn.description: Fed up with Donald Trump and his family's blatant profiteering, Americans dealt Republicans a resounding defeat in this month’s midterm elections. Democrats won by linking corruption to the cost-of-living crisis, but the party’s establishment remains compromised and must clean house before 2028.

proj-syn.title: The Fed's Risky Retreat From Transparency
proj-syn.description: Kevin Warsh, the new chair of the US Federal Reserve, is not wrong to abandon the practice of forward guidance. But if he continues to withhold information about how the central bank intends to assess the economic outlook and determine the appropriate stance of monetary policy, he is in for a rude awakening.

proj-syn.title: An Owl’s Guide to US-China Coexistence
proj-syn.description: In 2027 and beyond, the United States should lay the foundation for a stable coexistence with China, not a contest to “win.” A clear-eyed approach is needed to help make “the world safe for diversity,” as John F. Kennedy put it in 1963.

proj-syn.title: AI Investors Have Overlooked Obvious Risks
proj-syn.description: Prior to the US midterm elections on November 3, financial markets had been treating generative AI as some kind of unstoppable force that could not be hampered by higher interest rates or political and social resistance. But now reality may be setting in.

proj-syn.title: The Mismeasure of Privacy
proj-syn.description: Over the past few decades, we have adopted a new framework for thinking about privacy that centers our experience in the digital realm, conflates privacy with secrecy, and fails to account for the insecurity surveillance generates. As a result, even privacy advocates often undermine their own cause.

crunchbase.title: Crunchbase Data: Nvidia’s Startup Funding Deals Hit A Record. What’s Next After Huang?
crunchbase.description: Before it was thrust into crisis this week, Nvidia was steadily continuing its pace as one of the busiest startup investors around, including backing many of the biggest venture deals of 2026. We take a fresh look at where Nvidia and its venture arm NVentures have been investing and what the future could hold.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: Agentic AI And Infrastructure Are Still On A Roll
crunchbase.description: It was another big week for AI-related startup financings. Mirendil, a developer of agentic AI for R&D, led the pack with a $1 billion series A, followed by Mercor, which secured $750 million to connect AI developers with human experts.

crunchbase.title: Protein Startups Are Selling Lots Of Snacks And Drinks. Our Sample Tasting Found Most Neither Great Nor Horrible
crunchbase.description: As we chronicled earlier this week, both startups and established food brands are making it simpler than ever to up protein intake. From sodas to snack bars to ice cream, it’s now possible to get a fix of this coveted macronutrient with foods and drinks more commonly associated with sugar, starch and fat. But, do they taste good? To find out, we hit up a local Target for a selection of protein foods sold by venture-backed startups and subjected them to a taste test. Here are our findings.

crunchbase.title: How Founders Can Reduce Platform Risk Before It Threatens Growth
crunchbase.description: Founders should treat dependence on app stores as infrastructure risk, since a sudden removal can disrupt customer access, subscriptions and revenue with no reliable path to reinstatement. Sharing his experience, Yakov Filippenko, founder and CEO of Intch, suggests that building and testing alternative access and payment channels before a crisis can help keep the business operating.

crunchbase.title: VCs Are Still Chasing Protein, Even As Fake Meat Falls Out Of Favor
crunchbase.description: Recent startup investment has shifted away from meat substitutes and toward stuffing more protein into other packaged foods and drinks. It’s a fad that’s obvious on supermarket shelves, where startups and established brands alike relentlessly tout the added protein in their noodles, pancakes, cereals, energy bars, popcorn and so on. We take a look.

crunchbase.title: Exclusive: Nubank Alum Raises $14M For Colombia’s Palomma To Tackle Rent Payments, Landlord Financing
crunchbase.description: Colombia-based startup, Palomma, has raised $10 million in Series A funding led by Mexican venture firm Cometa to expand its financial services business for landlords, tenants and property managers, Crunchbase News has exclusively learned.

crunchbase.title: Anthropic Seeks Record $88.5B Tied To Public Market Debut
crunchbase.description: Anthropic is seeking to secure up to $88.5 billion in its planned IPO and a concurrent private placement, potentially making it the largest-ever fundraise tied to a public market debut. On Tuesday, the AI giant submitted an updated S-1 filing for its upcoming public offering, unveiling new details including a proposed share price range offering size.

crunchbase.title: The Crunchbase Unicorn Board Tops 1,900 Companies In October, With 34 Companies Joining — Half Under 4 Years Old
crunchbase.description: A total of 34 companies joined The Crunchbase Unicorn Board in October, adding more than $96 billion in value and $14.8 billion in total funding to the board. The board also reached a new record of 1,900 private companies last month, along with a new record for the U.S. with more than 1,000 private unicorn companies.

crunchbase.title: Startup Founders Are Using AI To File Patents. Here’s Where DIY Becomes A Liability.
crunchbase.description: AI can help startups reduce patent preparation costs, but DIY applications may overlook critical issues. In this guest commentary, attorneys Michael Drapkin and Nathan Mutter of AI-Native law firm Landfall IP, argue that combining AI with legal expertise can produce more efficient, commercially valuable patent protection that withstands investor scrutiny and is harder for competitors to circumvent.

crunchbase.title: Series A In 2026: Capital Is Flowing Faster, But Fewer Startups Are Making The Cut
crunchbase.description: More money is pouring into Series A rounds, but it isn’t opening the door to more startups. U.S. companies have raised $42 billion at that stage this year through October, up roughly 60% year over year, while deal counts remain on pace with the past few years, Crunchbase data shows.
